goal: Map the end-to-end latency chain from clicking the Projects-sidebar '+' (per-project NewChat row) to a usable Claude Code prompt in the new herdr tab, decomposed into sub-layers classified as algorithmic/architectural (herdr-fixable) vs external (claude CLI / MCP ecosystem), each anchored to file:line or URL evidence with a confidence-scored latency order-of-magnitude estimate.

ontology.type: end-to-end latency decomposition (causal pipeline: UI event -> client/server IPC -> in-process state machine -> OS process spawn -> external Node.js CLI cold start -> render feedback)
actors: herdr user (mouse click on Projects sidebar '+' / NewChat row)
herdr TUI thin client process (crossterm stdin reader, src/client/mod.rs)
herdr headless server process (AppState + event loop owner, src/server/headless.rs)
claude CLI child process (Node.js v24, Anthropic, spawned via portable-pty)
user's globally-configured MCP servers (33 entries in ~/.claude.json on this machine)
in_scope: Projects sidebar '+'/NewChat row hit-test and request_project_chat_tab flag (src/app/input/mouse.rs, src/app/input/sidebar.rs)
client<->server socket round trip for mouse input (src/protocol/wire.rs, src/client/mod.rs, src/server/headless.rs)
headless event-loop consumption of the deferred tab-open request (src/server/headless.rs run()/handle_deferred_requests_headless)
PTY spawn path: Workspace::create_tab_argv_command -> Pane::spawn_argv_command -> spawn_command_builder -> portable-pty (src/workspace.rs, src/pane.rs, src/pty/backend.rs, vendor/portable-pty)
first-render/attach pipeline for the new tab (render_dirty/render_notify, PtyIoActor poll loop)
Projects-tab session-list poll intervals (src/app/projects.rs) insofar as they could delay first paint
agent-detection background task (src/detect, src/pane.rs spawn_basic_detection_task) and whether it gates usability

out_of_scope: actually launching/timing a live `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` session in this repo (avoided: would consume the user's API/session budget and is not required to ground the claim; `claude --version` was used instead as a safe proxy for bare Node/CLI bootstrap cost)

components.name: TUI thin client input reader
components.role: Reads raw terminal mouse/key events via crossterm on a dedicated thread and forwards them to the server without local business logic. src/client/mod.rs (input thread ~L876, Unix send path ~L1467).

components.name: Client<->server wire protocol
components.role: Defines ClientMessage::Input/InputEvents and ClientInputEvent (incl. Mouse), and the raw_input conversion used server-side. src/protocol/wire.rs (L113, L253-301, L383).

components.name: Headless server event loop
components.role: Single-owner async loop (tokio multi-thread runtime) that drains client input, deferred requests, scheduled tasks, and drives rendering in a fixed step order each tick. src/server/headless.rs run() (L430-598), main.rs:744 confirms multi-thread runtime.

components.name: AppState Projects-sidebar mouse dispatch
components.role: Hit-tests the click against laid-out Projects-tab rows and routes to toggle_projects_row_at, which for the NewChat row queues a chat-tab request (or opens an agent-selector menu on Shift). src/app/input/mouse.rs (L547-564, L1030-1051), src/app/input/sidebar.rs (L236-296).

components.name: Deferred request flag: request_project_chat_tab
components.role: Option<ProjectChatTabRequest> field on AppState; set synchronously by the mouse handler, consumed synchronously later in the same loop tick by the server. src/app/state.rs:1448.

components.name: Project chat tab launch planner
components.role: Consumes the deferred request, builds argv/env for the chosen agent (claude --dangerously-skip-permissions [--resume <id>], ENABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1), and decides which workspace/tab to spawn into. src/app/projects.rs (L19-48 project_chat_launch, L144-260 handle_project_chat_tab_request/open_project_chat_tab_with_argv).

components.name: Workspace::create_tab_argv_command
components.role: Allocates a new Tab in the target Workspace and delegates PTY creation to Tab::new_argv_command. src/workspace.rs (L471-553).

components.name: Pane spawn (spawn_argv_command / spawn_command_builder)
components.role: Builds the CommandBuilder for argv, then synchronously spawns the PTY, wires the PtyIoActor reader, and spawns the per-pane agent-detection task. src/pane.rs (L1610-1649, L1795-1921).

components.name: portable-pty backend (vendored)
components.role: openpty() + slave.spawn_command(cmd): a synchronous fork()+exec() on Unix (forced by a pre_exec closure, which disables the posix_spawn fast path in Rust std). src/pty/backend.rs (L17-40), vendor/portable-pty/src/unix.rs (L228-286).

components.name: PtyIoActor (PTY reader thread)
components.role: Non-blocking fd + poll(2)-based edge-triggered reader; wakes render_notify as soon as bytes arrive, no fixed-interval sleep-poll. src/pty/actor/unix.rs (L344, L436).

components.name: Render/stream pipeline
components.role: render_dirty/render_notify-driven render_and_stream() step of the event loop; narrow settle-delays (20ms kitty-graphics; Windows-only cursor-settle) exist but do not apply to a freshly spawned CLI's first text output on Linux. src/server/headless.rs (L519-541), src/pane/terminal.rs (L40-41, L1133-1150).

components.name: claude CLI child process
components.role: External Node.js v24 application (Anthropic's Claude Code, v2.1.207 installed on this machine) launched via argv `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions [--resume <id>]` with ENABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1. Its own startup/readiness is outside herdr's control.

components.name: User's configured MCP servers
components.role: 33 entries in ~/.claude.json (globally configured, not project-scoped) that Claude Code connects to and tool-discovers at session startup by default.

components.name: Agent-detection background task
components.role: Per-pane tokio task on its own tick (500ms unidentified / 300ms identified / 50ms pending-release), reads only a screen-content snapshot; decoupled from the parser/viewport and from rendering by design. src/pane.rs (L1928-1963), src/detect/mod.rs, CLAUDE.md 'Detection is decoupled' principle.

components.name: Projects-tab session-list poll
components.role: Fingerprint-gated poll of the Claude session store to refresh the sidebar's chat list (2s baseline, hot-armed to 300ms for 10s right after a spawn). Governs when the new chat's title/marker appears in the LIST, not the new tab's own PTY rendering. src/app/projects.rs (L50-139).

claims.claim: A plain (non-Shift) left-click on a Projects-tab NewChat row synchronously sets AppState.request_project_chat_tab (session_id=None, default agent) in the same function call as the hit-test; Shift+click instead opens an agent-selector context menu without setting the flag.

herdr is client-server: mouse events are read by the thin client and forwarded immediately (no debounce/batching timer on the Unix send path) as ClientMessage::Input/InputEvents over a local socket before any AppState mutation happens server-side, where they are parsed via ClientInputEvent::to_raw_input_event and dispatched through route_client_events -> handle_mouse.

The request_project_chat_tab flag is consumed by handle_deferred_requests_headless in the SAME event-loop iteration in which drain_server_events processed the click (steps 5 then 6 of the fixed-order loop body), before the loop's render/stream step -- i.e. no extra loop-tick or timer delay is added between 'flag set' and 'tab spawn begins'.

Pane::spawn_command_builder calls crate::pty::backend::spawn_with_portable_pty(...) directly (synchronously) inside the async server-loop's task -- it is NOT dispatched via tokio::task::spawn_blocking, so the fork()+exec() call briefly occupies the tokio worker thread running the owning event loop.

The vendored portable-pty Unix backend spawns the child via std::process::Command with a pre_exec closure (session leader setup, TIOCSCTTY, fd cleanup); registering pre_exec forces Rust std onto the classic fork()+exec() path (posix_spawn cannot be used with an arbitrary pre_exec closure), which returns to the caller once fork()+exec() has been issued in the child, not once the child has finished initializing.

The actual wall-clock cost of this fork()+exec() call on this specific machine/repo build was not directly measured in this cartography session (no profiling/hyperfine run against the herdr binary, by scope: no herdr process start/stop was performed). Expected order of magnitude from general Linux fork/exec behavior is low-single-digit milliseconds, but this is an inference, not a measurement.

The only render-delay/debounce mechanisms on the PTY-bytes-processed path are KITTY_GRAPHICS_REDRAW_SETTLE (20ms, graphics-sequence-only) and a cursor-position-settle path that is compile-time disabled on non-Windows (CURSOR_POSITION_SETTLE_ENABLED = cfg!(windows)); ordinary text output from a freshly spawned CLI on Linux/macOS triggers immediate request_render with no delay.

PtyIoActor sets the master fd non-blocking and wakes via poll_pty_and_wake (poll(2)-based edge-triggered wait), not a fixed-interval sleep loop, so new child-process stdout is observed with near-zero added latency once written by the child.

open_project_chat_tab_with_argv switches to the new tab and sets Mode::Terminal synchronously, in the same call that creates the tab (before returning), so the FIRST render showing the new (still-empty) tab occurs in the same event-loop tick as the click -- this 'tab appeared' moment is distinct from and much earlier than 'Claude Code is usable'.

Agent detection runs as an independent per-pane tokio task with its own tick cadence (500ms unidentified / 300ms identified / 50ms pending-release) that only reads a screen-content snapshot; per herdr's own architectural principle ('Detection is decoupled... never touches the parser or viewport state'), it does not gate keyboard input or PTY-output rendering for the pane -- a user can already type into the new tab before agent detection has classified it.

Claude Code has been repeatedly and independently reported (multiple open/unresolved GitHub feature requests) to synchronously initialize and complete a tool-discovery handshake with ALL configured MCP servers before releasing the input prompt on interactive session start, adding 3-10+ seconds even with just 1-2 servers configured, with no shipped lazy-init mitigation for the reported cases; this specific machine has 33 MCP servers configured globally in ~/.claude.json (directly verified by reading the file in this session), which is well beyond the 1-2-server cases already reported to cost multiple seconds -- making Claude Code's own MCP-handshake cold start the most plausible dominant contributor to the user's 'too long until usable' complaint.

sources.url: file:///home/user/.claude.json#mcpServers (33 entries, read directly in this session)

claims.claim: `claude --version` (which almost certainly short-circuits before MCP initialization) returns in ~0.109s wall-clock on this machine, showing that Node.js runtime bootstrap + basic Claude Code CLI startup by itself is fast -- consistent with the hypothesis that the MCP tool-discovery handshake (not general Node.js/module-load cold start) is the specific mechanism responsible for multi-second-to-tens-of-seconds delays reported elsewhere for real sessions.

Node.js 22.8.0 added a new JS API for compile cache, module.enableCompileCache() (and the NODE_COMPILE_CACHE environment variable), enabling on-disk code caching of all modules loaded after the API call -- a built-in alternative to third-party v8-compile-cache packages, aimed at tooling and library authors, offering better performance and ESM support. Separately, an earlier nodejs/node pull request shipped V8 code cache changes to speed up Node's own startup. Both are documented, low-risk Node.js startup-performance mechanisms, but they target the module-compile/code-cache slice of cold start (a much smaller effect than the seconds-scale MCP tool-discovery handshake blocking described in cl11) -- so they are a complementary, not primary, mitigation for the '+' button latency.

Claude Code exposes a `--strict-mcp-config` flag that lets a caller supply an alternate (or empty) MCP config file, which the community documents as a workaround to skip the default global MCP set at startup, though it is officially described as inconvenient / not a first-class lazy-load feature (the ideal behavior -- MCP readiness never blocking the first prompt -- remains an open, unshipped feature request as of the referenced issues).

The exact wall-clock contribution of Layer 4 (this specific machine's `claude` cold start with 33 MCP servers configured) was NOT directly measured in this cartography session -- doing so would require actually launching a full `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` session and timing it, which was deliberately avoided (out of this session's read-only/no-process-start scope and to avoid unnecessary API/session cost). The dominance estimate in cl11 is an evidence-based inference (cross-referenced external reports + local MCP-count fact), not a direct profiling measurement of THIS repo/environment.

arm_projects_hot_poll() only shortens the Projects-tab session-LIST refresh interval (2s baseline -> 300ms for 10s) after a spawn, governing when the new chat's title/marker appears in the sidebar list; it does not gate or delay the new tab's own PTY attach/render/usability, which is driven independently by render_dirty/render_notify (cl7, cl8, cl9).

Aggregating cl1, cl4, cl5, cl7, cl8, cl9 (each directly grounded in source code with no discovered sleep/debounce/extra-tick on the critical path), herdr's OWN internal pipeline from click to 'new (empty) tab visible and PTY-attached' completes within a single event-loop iteration and is architecturally bounded to low-single-digit milliseconds (well under one render frame budget) under normal system load -- i.e. herdr's own code is very unlikely to be the dominant source of the reported 'too long until usable' delay; the delay the user perceives is attributable almost entirely to the external claude CLI/MCP cold start (cl11).
